notes: This contract records public C++ TCK witnesses for IEEE 1516.1-2025 §12.13.5 one-transport-connection/one-federate-session behavior, bounded §12.13.4.1 Session ID and sequence-number behavior, and bounded §12.13.4.3/§12.13.4.6 protocol behavior. The transport adapter checks a CTRL_HEARTBEAT originates at the federate and that every observed heartbeat receives a matching CTRL_HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE using its response-to sequence, connection, and session. It also checks one CTRL_NEW_SESSION_STATUS for each received CTRL_NEW_SESSION and that each sequential HLA_CALL_RESPONSE acknowledges the HLA_CALL_REQUEST sequence on its connection. The termination extension checks one federate-to-RTI CTRL_CLOSE and one matching RTI-to-federate CTRL_CLOSE_ACK on each session; the C++ assertion requires the acknowledgement to echo the request sequence in Last Received Message Number and the federate-side transport close to occur afterward. After each public Disconnect, the adapter sends a valid Table 34 CTRL_RESUME_REQUEST using that terminated Session ID. The C++ case requires the RTI to close each probe socket without returning a Resume Status, directly witnessing that the old ID is invalid and the session is purged under §12.13.4.3 p. 399 l. 59, as well as the invalid-Session-ID socket closure under §12.13.4.6 p. 408 l. 86. The TCK creates two independent RTIambassador sessions and uses the official connect, join, service, resign, destroy, and disconnect APIs. Its current-process adapter uses a transparent loopback proxy to count client TCP connections and inspect standard-defined transport headers. The C++ case asserts zero Session IDs in New Session requests, distinct nonzero opaque IDs in successful New Session Status responses, one request/status pair on each of two connections, valid strictly increasing sequence numbers on observed messages (allowing the invalid-sequence exception for CTRL_NEW_SESSION and the specified wrap), and request/response sequence correspondence for its bounded sequential service path. Pipelined requests are not covered. A separate public C++ TCK case exercises RTIambassador connect/disconnect against a byte-independent peer: it checks literal New Session request and Status frames and the Table 35 version payload, then the federate-side RTI client emits zero-payload Table 34 CTRL_HEARTBEAT messages in the specified direction after FED_INT_HEART is configured to 0.1 seconds through public configuration. Across four complete sessions the first client heartbeat arrived 106–118 ms after New Session Status, and every observed client heartbeat carried the invalid Last Received Message Number sentinel because no HLA service message had occurred. The independent peer responds with a matching CTRL_HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE for each client heartbeat, then acknowledges Close; the client uses increasing sequence numbers through its Close and closes after the acknowledgement. This directly witnesses §12.13.4.5 p. 403 l. 31, l. 55, l. 70, and l. 76, and §12.13.4.5.3 p. 405 l. 16, only for this finite public-API protocol slice; it does not establish heartbeat response behavior by the RTI server, rollover, full message-history behavior, RTI-side ID assignment, all Table 33/34 messages, independent-provider federation interoperability, or conformance. This is bounded evidence for the tested provider only; it does not establish independent-provider conformance or complete conformance.

api_surfaces.signature: Two RTIambassador instances connect, join distinct federates, perform a service, resign, and disconnect; an adapter observes TCP connection count, heartbeat and session-termination request/response sequence correlation, response-before-client-close ordering, and standard-defined transport headers, while C++ assertions check Session IDs and sequence-number progression
